guidance.heading: Guidance and Outlook
section: Spire expects fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings to be in the range of $5.05–$5.25 per share, compared with its previous guidance range of $5.40–$5.60 per share. The updated outlook primarily reflects recent regulatory outcomes in Tennessee and Alabama, as well as updated assumptions for weather-normalized margin recovery in Missouri, including continued exposure to variability in fiscal 2027.

Looking ahead, Spire expects fiscal 2028 adjusted earnings per share of $6.10–$6.30 and has increased its long-term adjusted EPS compound annual growth rate target to 6%–8% through fiscal 2031, using the fiscal 2028 guidance midpoint of $6.20 per share as a base. The long-term growth outlook includes earnings from the Spire MoGas expansion project, which are expected to begin during construction, ahead of the project's targeted in-service date in fiscal 2030.

Spire has also increased its 10-year capital investment plan to $11.8 billion through fiscal 2036, supporting continued investment in its regulated utility infrastructure and long-term growth. Capital expenditures in fiscal 2027 are expected to total $880 million.

desk.period: Q4 fiscal 2026 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026) and full fiscal year
desk.headline: Full-year adjusted EPS up 20% to $4.02; seasonal Q4 adjusted loss of $0.99; FY27 guidance cut to $5.05–5.25, FY28 set at $6.10–6.30

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted, continuing operations (Q4); GAAP diluted EPS -$1.60 vs -$0.89

results: Fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS rose 20% to $4.02, helped by new rates in Missouri and Alabama; GAAP EPS from continuing operations fell to $2.62 on deal costs.
The September quarter is seasonally loss-making: the adjusted loss widened to $0.99 a share from $0.69 on higher depreciation, interest and operating costs. Q4 revenue rose to $339.4m from $281.4m.
Spire finished becoming a pure regulated gas utility: it bought Piedmont's Tennessee business and sold its marketing and storage units (a $257.6m after-tax gain).
Debt rose to fund the Tennessee deal: long-term debt was $5.74bn vs $3.37bn a year earlier.
Quarterly dividend raised 4.8% to $0.865, the 24th straight yearly increase.

guidance.summary: Spire cut its fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS range to $5.05–5.25 from $5.40–5.60, citing rate decisions in Tennessee and Alabama and weaker Missouri usage. It set fiscal 2028 at $6.10–6.30 and raised its long-term EPS growth target to 6–8% a year through 2031.

points: The Tennessee rate decision capped margin growth more tightly than expected, which management called a temporary issue; it was also disappointed with the Alabama outcome.
Missouri weather-adjusted margin recovery came in about $24m short in fiscal 2026, and some weather drag is expected again in 2027.
Fiscal 2028 is seen as a more normal earnings base once new Missouri and Tennessee rates apply; a Missouri case asking for a $228m increase has been filed.
The MoGas pipeline expansion, fully funded by Ameren Missouri, should add about $15m a year of earnings once running in fiscal 2030.
New share issuance needs are small, about $0–50m a year through 2031.

watch: Progress of the Missouri rate case (decision expected late fiscal 2027) and the Tennessee filing in 2027.
Missouri weather-normalised margin recovery during the 2026–27 winter.
Balance-sheet strength after the Tennessee acquisition debt.
